source_note: Chain wear limits from Park Tool's own repair-help article, fetched and read on 2026-10-25. This is the first web-sourced batch: the citation carries source_url and retrieved_at, because a web page changes while a printed page does not. Every other row of the research data sheet was discarded - see docs/RESEARCH_FINDINGS.md.

nodes.name: Chain
nodes.description: The chain is a consumable part of the drivetrain; its rivets and rollers wear with use, which shows up as apparent stretching and causes poor meshing with cogs and chainrings.

evidence.quote: Chains are a consumable part of the bicycle drivetrain.

nodes.name: Chain wear replacement limit
nodes.description: The wear value at which a chain should be replaced, by drivetrain class: 1.0% for single-speed, 0.75% for a 10-speed cassette/freewheel or less, 0.5% for 11-speed or more. The publisher states these are general guidelines and that each manufacturer has its own specification.

evidence.quote: Drivetrain Wear Single-speed 1.0% 10-speed cassette/freewheel or less 0.75% 11-speed cassette or more 0.5%

edges.claim: The chain meshes with the cassette cogs; wear makes it mesh poorly, causing poor shifting and premature cog wear.

evidence.quote: This wear can cause the chain to mesh poorly with cogs and chainrings, causing poor shifting and premature wear to the cogs.

edges.claim: A chain is replaced when it reaches the wear limit for its drivetrain class: 1.0% single-speed, 0.75% up to 10-speed, 0.5% for 11-speed or more.
conditions: General guidance: each manufacturer specifies its own limit

evidence.quote: Your chain should be replaced by the time it reaches the wear value specified.
